title: Fiducia not act of absolute faith but included in living formed faith (credere in Deum)
source_text: XXXIX. Quum autem docent fiduciam non esse partem sive actum fidei, loquuntur de fide absolute spectata, & secundum propriam naturam, non vero de fide viva, quam formatam appellant, & quam solam actu servare & justificare concedunt, cujusque actus exprimitur per credere in Deum. Fides enim hoc modo considerata fiduciam includit, & fiducia inter illius actus numerari debet, ut & ipsa dilectio Dei, ex confessione Doctorum Ecclesiae Romanae. Licet secundum eorum doctrinam, dilectio non sit actus fidei simpliciter spectatae, & prout est virtus a charitate distincta. Qua de re videndus est Jaubertus Arelatensis Archiepiscopus, in Clypeo fidei Catholicae, contra Molinaei Clypeum, Tom. 1. capite 40. Ubi pluries affirmat & repetit fiduciam & dilectionem includi in fide viva, & fidem vivam constare non solum assensu qui praebetur veritati divinae, sed etiam fiducia quae ex charitate manat. Praesertim numero 8, 9, & 11. ubi etiam observat, neminem esse Doctorum Catholicorum qui non admittat in fide cognitionem aliquam supernaturalem, & in fide viva fiduciam divinae misericordiae, & qui non fateatur Deo injurium esse qui credit Deo, nec tamen in eum sperat, & eum diligit. Quomodo etiam Lombardus verbis Augustini dicit, quod credere in Deum est credendo amare, credendo in eum ire, credendo ei adhaerere, & membris ejus incorporari. Lib. 3. Sententiarum, Distinctione 23.
pass_a_gloss: When they teach that trust is not a part or act of faith, they speak of faith absolutely considered and according to its proper nature, not of living faith, which they call formed, and which alone they grant actually saves and justifies, and whose act is expressed by believing in God. For faith considered in this way includes trust, and trust ought to be numbered among its acts, as also the very love of God, by the confession of the doctors of the Roman Church. Yet according to their doctrine love is not an act of faith simply considered, and insofar as faith is a virtue distinct from charity. On this see Jaubert Archbishop of Arles, in the Catholic Shield of Faith against Molinaeus Shield, Tom. 1, chapter 40, where he often affirms and repeats that trust and love are included in living faith, and that living faith consists not only in the assent given to divine truth but also in the trust that flows from charity. Especially at numbers 8, 9, and 11 he also observes that there is no Catholic doctor who does not admit some supernatural cognition in faith, and in living faith trust of divine mercy, and who does not confess that the one who believes God yet does not hope in him and love him does God injury. So also Lombard in Augustine words says that to believe in God is by believing to love, by believing to go into him, by believing to cling to him, and to be incorporated into his members (Lib. 3 Sent., Dist. 23).
pass_b_english: When Romans say fiducia is not a faith-act, they mean absolute faith in its proper nature, not living formed faith (credere in Deum), which alone actually saves and which includes fiducia and love among its acts.

Jaubert (Clypeus 1.40.8-11) and Lombard via Augustine: living faith is not assent alone but also mercy-trust flowing from charity; believing in God means loving, going into, clinging, and being incorporated into his members.

lemmas.latin: fiduciam & dilectionem includi in fide viva
lemmas.gloss: that trust and love are included in living faith

choices.why: Fiducia belongs here, not to absolute faith.
rejected: fiducia as act of absolute/unformed faith
